chunks: From him, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, all together, from Ibn Mahboub, from Is'haq ibn Jareer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

When a man is not watchful of guarding the honour of his wife or those married to him, so he does not act with a sense of honour, Allah Mighty and Majestic sends a bird called Al-Qanfadar to him which settles upon a joist of his door, then gives him respite for forty days. Then it shouts out, 'Allah is most Honourable and Loves every honourable one'. So either he (starts) acting vigilantly, and changes and shows remorse to his lack of protectionism, otherwise it flies over until it settles upon his head, so it spreads out its wings upon his eyes, then it flies away. So Allah Mighty and Majestic snatches away from him, after that, the spirit of the 'Eman' (faith), and the Angels name him as the cuckold (pimp).

key_terms.الدَّيُّوثُ: A man who lacks ghayrah and is indifferent to the honour of his family
key_terms.الْغَيْرَةُ: Sense of honour or protectiveness, particularly regarding family
key_terms.الْقَفَنْدَرُ: A specific bird mentioned in the hadith that serves as a divine sign
key_terms.رُوحَ الْإِيمَانِ: The spirit of faith, which is removed from the person
key_terms.مَنَاكِحُهُ: His wives or those married to him

ai.seo_question: What is the consequence of lacking ghayrah (sense of honour) in a man according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the divine mechanism of 'ghayrah' by describing the angelic bird Al-Qanfadar as a tangible warning sign for a man who neglects protecting his family's honor. Scholarly tradition interprets the forty-day period as a grace period for repentance, after which the loss of 'ruh al-iman' (spirit of faith) results in the specific title 'al-dayyuth,' highlighting the spiritual gravity of passive negligence in domestic guardianship. This narrative underscores the Shia emphasis on active moral vigilance as a core component of faith.

en.hubeali:
From him, and Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, altogether, from Ibn Mahboub, from Is’haq Bin Jareer, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘When a man is not watchful of guarding the honour of his wife or those married to him, so he does not act with a sense of honour, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Sends a bird called Al-Qanfadar to him which settles upon a joist of his door, then gives him respite for forty days. Then it shouts out, ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> is most Honourable and Loves every honourble one’. So either he (starts) acting vigilantly, and changes and shows remorse to his lack of protectionism, otherwise it flies over until it settles upon his head, so it spreads out its wings upon his eyes, then it files away. So Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Snatches away from him, after that, the spirit of the ‘Eman’ (faith), and the Angels name him as the cuckold (pimp)’.
en.sarwar: 3. It is narrated from the narrator of the previous Hadith Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa all from ibn Mahbub from Ishaq ibn Jarir who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

When a man’s vigilance is shaken in matters of protection for his family and wife or those married to him, like his slave-girl, but does not act vigilantly, Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, sends a bird called al-Qafandar which sits on the upper portion of his door and gives him forty days and calls him saying, ‘Allah is vigilant and loves vigilant people.’ If he then acts vigilantly, changes and dislikes what has shaken his sense of protectionism, otherwise, the bird flies, sits on his head and hangs its wings on his eyes; then Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, removes the spirit of belief and faith from him and the angels call him a pimp.’”
